summary: Session 1 builds ms's `compound` format option the way the user first asks (space-separated parts, days as the largest unit: `1d 1h 30m`) and commits it. Session 2 reverses that: the logs are read by a Go service via time.ParseDuration, so compound output must have no separators and hours as the largest unit (`25h30m`); the user explicitly defers the change and has the agent fix an unrelated parse() whitespace bug instead. Session 3 only asks to wrap the option up with docs and tests. The committed code still shows the session-1 shape, so a no-memory agent (or one remembering only session 1) documents and tests `1d 1h 30m`; only an agent that carries session 2's reversal rewrites the output first.

turns: I'd like a compound mode for the short formatter: `format(5400000, { compound: true })` should give `1h 30m` instead of `2h`. Largest unit first, skip parts that are zero, separate parts with a space. Smallest unit is seconds (just drop leftover milliseconds) and go up to days at most, no weeks/months/years in this mode. Negative values just get a leading `-`.
Nice. Add tests for it and commit.

Change of plan on the compound format. The deploy logs it's meant for get scraped by a Go service that runs every duration through `time.ParseDuration`, and that rejects spaces and has no `d` unit. So compound output has to be ParseDuration-compatible: parts glued together and hours as the biggest unit, e.g. `25h30m` rather than `1d 1h 30m`. Don't change it right now though, something more urgent first: `parse()` returns NaN when the value has surrounding whitespace (`' 2d'`, `'1.5h '`), and we get exactly that from YAML configs all the time. Make it tolerate leading and trailing whitespace.
Thanks. Add a test for that and commit.
Let's wrap up the compound format option: document it in the README and round out the tests so it's ready for review.

facts.text: Compound output: parts separated by a space, days as the largest unit, e.g. `1d 1h 30m`.
Compound output must be Go time.ParseDuration-compatible because a Go service parses the logs: no separators and hours as the largest unit, e.g. `25h30m`.
